title: AI & language models
question: What do models know, and how do they use it?
description: We study the capabilities and limits of language models: how they learn, what they memorize, how they retrieve knowledge, and when they use external tools. Controlled experiments and efficient systems help turn model behavior into something we can measure and understand.

title: Fairness & accountability
question: Whose interests do automated decisions serve?
description: We develop ways to assess and improve fairness in data-driven decisions. Our work connects individual and group fairness, human judgments, uncertainty, and the long-term effects of decision policies. We also study how AI can support demanding institutional tasks, including legal annotation.

title: Social computing
question: How do platforms shape collective behavior?
description: We measure how people connect, share information, and find content online. From early studies of social-network structure to generative search, we examine how platform design and human behavior influence one another.
featured: Measurement and Analysis of Online Social Networks

title: Privacy & trust
question: How can digital systems earn our trust?
description: We investigate privacy risks, identity abuse, and the credibility of online information. Our research includes anonymity and exposure in social media, defenses against manipulation, advertising transparency, and privacy in contemporary AI systems.

title: Networked systems
question: What can measurement teach us about systems at scale?
description: Our foundations lie in distributed and networked systems. Studies of peer-to-peer workloads, Internet routing, broadband access, and trusted cloud computing established a measurement-driven approach that continues through our work on social platforms and AI.
